授業科目の目的・目標・履修条件について.授業科目の目的（英語）: This course will introduce students to some of the main topics in applied ethics, from the perspectives of Anglo-American ethical theories such as ultilitarianism and virtue ethics, though non-European philosophical perspectives like Confucianism will also be considered. Students will read short extracts from philosophical articles giving contrasting points of view on ethical topics such as abortion, euthanasia, animal rights and the morality of torture, discussing these issues in class and writing about them. This course is also designed for students who are also still learning academic English.
授業科目の目的・目標・履修条件について.履修条件: This course is designed for students who are still learning English, as well as for students with high fluency and native English speaking abilities. Students with higher English fluency may be asked to take leadership roles in group discussion activities.

授業の内容（90分授業＝2時間）
事前/事後学修の内容
rows: How to argue philosophically, the structure of an argument, exercises on simple ethical topics
Summarizing some of the main ideas of Immanuel Kant's thought on ethics
Summarizing the main ideas of John Stuart Mill's ideas on ethics
Summarizing the main ideas of Alasdair Macintyre on ethics
Investigating the main pro-life and pro-choice philosophical perspectives on abortion
Investigating the major utilitarian arguments in favour of euthanasia
Investigating the major Christian and medical ethical objections to legalizing euthanasia
Investigating the deontological arguments in favor of animal rights to life and freedom from captivity
Investigating philosophical perspectives against the concept of animal rights
Investigating arguments for civil disobedience from the anti-slavery and 20th century civil rights campaigns
Investigating arguments against civil obedience from ancient and modern philosophers
Investigating legal and philosophical arguments in favor of legislation against hate speech
Investigating philosophical arguments on freedom of speech and limited regulation of hate speech
Investigating philosophical and economic arguments against the social responsibility of business
Investigating arguments for the compatibility of ethical conduct with good business practice
textbook reading, writing, revising and submitting essay
